tool.title: 2026 Uttarakhand helicopter crash
tool.excerpt: On 30 October 2026, a Airbus Helicopters H125 operated by Trans Bharat aviation crashed near Joshimath, India. == Accident == The Helicopter involved in the accident took off from Badrinath at around 1.14 pm for and was Sahastradhara helipad in Dehradun. Badrinath is an important pilgrimage center during the Char Dham yatra for Hindus. The Helicopter was flying in heavy snowfall when contact was lost near Hathi Parvat. When the helicopter failed to reach its destination, two teams from the Indian Army,the Indo-Tibetian Border Police, the district administration and SDRF were mobilised to conduct search and rescue operations, when an Indian Army observation post reported a stray helicopter flying into a valley about one kilometre above the Ghanta Khad temple near Pandukeshwar. Two IAF helicopters and Drones were mobilised and located the crash site in a densly forested area near Chaien village in Joshimath. The difficult climate and high altitude of Uttarakhand is notorious for causing multiple Helicopter crashes in India. Previous crashes had occurred in the region in June 2025 and October 2022. As a pre-caution, all the helicopter fleet of Trans Bharat were temporarily grounded. == Casualties == There were five passengers from Karnataka on board the flight, who were identified as Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K and HS Natraja. The helicopter was pioleted by Captain Himanshu Sabarwal. All six were killed in the crash. Fake claims, backed by Pakistani accounts spread on social media portraying it as a terrorist attack on an aircraft carrying the family of Lieutenant General Sanjay Mitra. == Investigation == India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau was reported to have launched an Investigation into the accident. == See Also == 2026 Baramati Learjet 45 crash 2011 Pawan Hans Mi-17 crash == References ==
